top_five.text: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is experiencing its largest Ebola outbreak on record, with 5,198 deaths and 10,668 confirmed cases across eight provinces amid a lack of licensed vaccines.
An Allied Democratic Forces militant attack on a health clinic in North Kivu killed up to 44 people and dispersed confirmed and suspected Ebola patients into local communities.
Saudi-led coalition air strikes killed at least 33 people near Sanaa following Houthi ballistic missile strikes targeting Riyadh's financial district.
Winter storms submerged displacement camps in sewage and rainwater across the Gaza Strip, threatening 200,000 dilapidated tents alongside continued airstrikes.
An estimated 28 million people in Afghanistan live in poverty following prolonged drought and the return of 2.9 million refugees over the past year.

top_story.quote: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is confronting an unprecedented Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo strain, recording 5,198 deaths among 10,668 confirmed cases while violent attacks on health facilities sever containment lines.
top_story.label: AFRICA — DRC Ebola Outbreak

Middle East.headline: Gaza/OPT — Winter storms flood displacement camps amid ongoing military strikes
Middle East.body: Torrential rainfall flooded displacement camps across the Gaza Strip, particularly in Deir al-Balah, submerging tents, destroying essential belongings, and exposing displaced families to sewage overflow. Human rights organizations warned of an escalating crisis, stating that approximately 200,000 tents are dilapidated and incapable of providing adequate shelter against winter conditions. Simultaneously, continued Israeli military attacks over a 48-hour period resulted in the deaths of six to ten Palestinians, according to local health officials.
verified_figures: At least 6 to 10 Palestinians killed in strikes over 48 hours

Middle East.headline: Yemen/Saudi Arabia — Coalition air strikes kill dozens near Sanaa following Houthi missile launch
Middle East.body: Air strikes conducted by the Saudi-led coalition killed at least 33 people near Sanaa, Yemen. Following the coalition bombardment, Houthi rebels launched two ballistic missiles targeting the financial district in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Saudi forces intercepted both incoming missiles, but falling debris caused structural damage to the Aramco Tower in the capital.
verified_figures: At least 33 people killed in air strikes near Sanaa

Americas.headline: Haiti — Gang leader Mathias Saintil killed in security operations
Americas.body: Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé announced the death of Mathias Saintil, leader of the Boston gang operating in Cité Soleil, Port-au-Prince. According to human rights monitoring cited by local reports, Saintil died in a hospital from abdominal injuries sustained during a drone strike in the Boston area. The killing occurred amid intensified security operations involving Salvadoran personnel deployed after four Salvadoran aviation technicians serving with an international Gang Suppression Force were kidnapped on 18 October.

Americas.headline: Haiti — 400 Mawozo gang requests UN dialogue and ceasefire
Americas.body: The 400 Mawozo gang, one of Haiti's major armed groups, sent a written statement to a national dismantling agency and appealed to the United Nations Secretary-General to send a delegation to Haiti for dialogue and reconciliation. The group, accused by the UN and human rights organizations of widespread killing, rape, and kidnapping, described the outreach as a push to preserve human lives. The request follows a similar appeal made by gang leader Wilson Joseph on 1 November.

Americas.headline: Venezuela — Collapse of 15 housing towers following dual earthquakes
Americas.body: An engineering analysis following two powerful earthquakes in Venezuela pointed to possible building-code violations in five public housing complexes where 15 residential towers collapsed. Technical experts noted that structural defects likely increased the risk of failure, though direct causation remains under investigation. Emergency search efforts have taken place across damaged structures, including a collapsed 13-story tower where missing residents were reported buried beneath rubble.

Americas.headline: Colombia — Three soldiers killed in drone strike on military base
Americas.body: A drone attack targeting a military base in Colombia has left three soldiers dead. Further details regarding the perpetrators, the exact location of the base, or broader operational impacts were not immediately released in preliminary reporting.

Africa.headline: DR Congo — Ebola outbreak reaches record 5,198 deaths amid rapid spread
Africa.body: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is experiencing the largest Ebola outbreak in its history, caused by the Bundibugyo virus strain. According to World Health Organization figures as of 3 November, the country recorded 10,668 confirmed cases and 5,198 deaths across eight provinces, representing a 48.7 percent case fatality ratio. Active transmission persists across 51 health zones, with 2,881 recorded recoveries. UN officials warned that the outbreak is expanding faster than containment capacities. Response efforts remain severely hampered by a lack of licensed vaccines targeting the Bundibugyo strain.

Africa.headline: DR Congo — Militant attack on North Kivu clinic kills dozens and disperses Ebola patients
Africa.body: Militants affiliated with Islamic State and the Allied Democratic Forces raided the village of Cantine-Aloya in North Kivu province, setting fire to a health facility and killing between 33 and 44 people. The assault forced patients and staff to flee. Local health officials confirmed that those dispersed included one confirmed Ebola patient and five suspected cases, three of whom are high-risk contacts. The flight of infected individuals into surrounding communities creates severe risks of accelerating Ebola transmission in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Russian Air Attacks Target Energy Infrastructure and Cause Mass Power Outages
Europe.body: Massive Russian drone and missile strikes targeted Ukrainian energy infrastructure and residential areas, causing severe electricity disruptions across multiple regions. Ukrainian officials stated Russian forces launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, causing damage in Kyiv and other parts of the country. Attacks in Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv cut power to approximately 850,000 people. At least nine people were wounded in the strikes, while reporting also indicated Russian forces targeted emergency crews responding to a strike location in southern Ukraine.

Europe.headline: Poland — Nine Dead and 16 Wounded in Kraków Terrorist Shooting
Europe.body: Polish authorities initiated a terrorism investigation after a gunman opened fire in Kraków's central market square, killing six people and wounding up to 16 others. Police subsequently discovered three additional bodies inside the suspect's residence. The suspect, identified as a Polish citizen holding radical far-right views, used an automatic firearm before being shot and apprehended by police. Foreign nationals from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal, and Russia were among the casualties, including one British citizen who was killed.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Afghanistan — Deepening Poverty and Population Returns
Asia-Pacific.body: A new United Nations Development Programme report indicates that Afghanistan's humanitarian crisis deepened in 2025, leaving an estimated 28 million people living in poverty. The crisis is driven by prolonged drought, declining international assistance, and mass population returns. Approximately 2.9 million Afghans returned to the country during the year, pushing an additional 1.4 million people into severe economic hardship despite modest national GDP growth.
verified_figures: 28 million people living in poverty in 2025
1.4 million additional people pushed into hardship

Asia-Pacific.headline: Thailand/China — Protection Risks and Forced Deportations of Uyghur Refugees
Asia-Pacific.body: Human rights activists warn that two Uyghur men currently detained in Thailand face severe risks of torture and abuse if deported to China. The warning follows the forced deportation of 40 Uyghur men from Thailand to China last year, despite offers from the United States and Canada to resettle them. The United Nations noted that the whereabouts of those previously returned remain unknown.
verified_figures: 40 Uyghur men forcibly deported to China last year

Asia-Pacific.headline: Myanmar — Armed Conflict Impacts Mental Health and Agricultural Labor
Asia-Pacific.body: A cross-sectional study of 1,504 hired agricultural workers in Myanmar demonstrates that exposure to active armed conflict leads to heightened absenteeism and lower labor productivity. Published in BMC Global and Public Health, the research identifies psychological trauma as the primary mechanism through which political violence impairs worker performance among vulnerable rural populations.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Democratic Republic of the Congo — Ebola Outbreak Complicated by Vaccine Shortages
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is responding to an outbreak of the Ebola Bundibugyo strain, for which there is currently no licensed vaccine. Health specialists report that vaccine shortages and epidemiological barriers are complicating response efforts, forcing researchers to accelerate testing for multi-purpose vaccines. The Bundibugyo strain previously caused epidemics in Uganda in 2007 and the DRC in 2012, but previous research opportunities were not fully capitalized on, leaving health systems without a specific preventative tool during the current outbreak.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Japan — 5.7-Magnitude Earthquake Injures at Least 22 in Central Prefectures
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: A 5.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Japan early on 8 November, injuring at least 22 people across Shizuoka and Aichi prefectures. The tremor's epicenter was located in western Shizuoka at a depth of approximately 40 kilometers. Strong shaking shattered shop windows, damaged several structures, and forced the temporary suspension of local and bullet train services. No tsunami warning was issued, and operators confirmed no abnormalities at the Hamaoka nuclear power plant. Meteorological officials noted this was the third major earthquake to hit Japan this month.
